verdict: Huntington's revenue jumped 31% as the Cadence and Veritex deals made it a much bigger bank, though acquisition costs and a larger share count held EPS at $0.33.

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: The spread between interest earned on loans and securities and interest paid on deposits — a bank's core revenue.

segments.name: Noninterest income
segments.note: Fees: service charges, cards, capital markets, wealth and other customer fees.

opex.name: Noninterest expense
opex.note: People, branches, technology and other running costs, including acquisition-related expenses.

follow100Note: For a bank, the 'direct cost' in this chart is the provision for credit losses — money set aside for loans that may not be repaid. Kept as profit is income after tax of $724 million; $721 million is attributable to Huntington and $680 million to common shareholders after preferred dividends.

takeaways.title: Interest income surged on scale
takeaways.text: Net interest income rose 37% to $2.07 billion as the Cadence and Veritex acquisitions added loans and deposits, and the margin widened to 3.25%.

takeaways.title: Adjusted EPS excludes deal costs
takeaways.text: Excluding notable items, mostly acquisition-related expenses worth $0.05 a share, adjusted EPS was $0.38 and adjusted return on tangible common equity was 16.6%.

takeaways.title: Charge-offs rose
takeaways.text: Net charge-offs increased to $146 million from $75 million a year ago, a credit cost to watch as the combined loan book seasons.

oneTimers: GAAP results include notable items, mainly Cadence/Veritex acquisition-related expenses, worth about $0.05 per share after tax; adjusted EPS of $0.38 excludes them.
footerNote: Bank accounting differs from other industries: revenue is net interest income plus fees, and the provision for credit losses is shown as the direct cost.
